# Heroes

> Heroes is a small compiled programming language designed so that every
> plausible LLM mistake is a compile error. Made for LLMs, yet plain to human
> eyes: no null, no exceptions, no implicit conversions, no standard library:
> everything comes from C through an FFI that clang verifies against the real
> headers. The compiler is written in Heroes and reproduces itself byte for
> byte: asked to compile itself it writes out the very C file the repository
> ships, and `cmp` finds nothing between them.

The entire language specification is deliberately small, measured at 3592
tokens against a hard ceiling of 4096, because the spec is the prompt, not
documentation. If you are a language model asked to write Heroes, read the
spec first; it is the whole language:

- [The specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giuseppearici/heroes-lang/main/spec/heroes-spec.md): the whole language in ~3592 tokens, written to be your prompt

Ground rules a generated program must respect: exactly one way to write
anything (a canonical formatter; 4-space indentation, tabs are errors); named
arguments are mandatory where two parameters share a type; `match` is
exhaustive and `_` is forbidden on variants; failure is a value (`T?`,
`ok`/`fail`/`?`), there is no null and there are no exceptions; `???` is a
legal expression that reports what belongs in the gap instead of failing.

## Pages

- [Home](https://heroes-lang.org/index.html): what the language is, one real sample, the claim
- [Why Heroes](https://heroes-lang.org/why.html): the founding constraint (no standard library), the thesis, the cost formula, the objections answered
- [Self-hosted](https://heroes-lang.org/selfhost.html): the fixpoint, 165 modules and 48,342 lines of Heroes emitting byte-identical C, and one C file per module with a build cache keyed on the headers it read
- [The Zen](https://heroes-lang.org/zen.html): twenty lines the binary prints from `heroes this`
- [The panel](https://heroes-lang.org/panel.html): how a change to the language is decided, five judges with differentiated briefs and four vetoes, the historian's seat, and what the design borrowed from Hylo, Swift, Cyclone, Go, Nim, Zig, Ada, Pascal and the rest
- [The author](https://heroes-lang.org/author.html): Giuseppe Arici, partner and CTO at Codermine in Brescia, author of *Heroes of code*, a history of programming languages framed as a dream journey with David Bowie as the guide, out on 20 September 2026. He had never written a compiler before this one
- [Build log](https://heroes-lang.org/log.html): one postcard per milestone, newest first
- [Thanks](https://heroes-lang.org/thanks.html): the designers of every language Heroes borrowed from, named one by one, with what each borrowing was; links go to English Wikipedia only where an article about that person was verified to exist
- [Documentation](https://heroes-lang.org/docs/index.html): the language page by page; every code block is a slice of a repository file that compiles and runs
- [Errors](https://heroes-lang.org/errors.html): part of the documentation and linked from its landing page: diagnostics as a deliverable, real output with machine-applicable fixes tagged `certain`, and the per-mistake catch rates against a control build (a dropped argument label 76% vs 0%, a shadowed name 94% vs 0%, a lazy catch-all 100% vs 63%)

Every page above also exists in Italian under `/it/`, same filenames
(https://heroes-lang.org/it/index.html and so on), linked from each page's
`hreflang` alternates. The two editions are written independently rather than
machine-translated; code, compiler output and the twenty Zen lines are identical
in both, because they are quotations of real files and real output.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/giuseppearici/heroes-lang): the compiler, the spec, the design record; build with `clang -I runtime seed/heroes.c runtime/runtime.c -o heroes`, then `./heroes run examples/gallery/00-first.hero`
- [Examples](https://github.com/giuseppearici/heroes-lang/tree/main/examples/gallery): twelve small programs, one per language idea; every code block on the site is anchored to one of these files, in the canonical form `heroes fmt` prints

## Notes

- Status: built in the open, not packaged. The fixpoint is measured; the
  bootstrap compiler is archived and no longer builds; there is no installer,
  and the way in is a C compiler and one command.
- Diagnostics are machine-readable: `heroes check --json` emits schema 1 with
  stable snake_case codes, spans, notes and fixes.
